name: Potatoes
summary: Chit earlies from late winter, plant through spring, and lift new potatoes from June or maincrops from August.
description: When to plant seed potatoes in the UK: chit from late January, first earlies in late March, second earlies in April, maincrops to early May. RHS timings.
intro: Potatoes are grown from seed potatoes, which are small tubers sold for planting, not from a packet of seed. In the UK the job is spread across spring: first earlies around late March, second earlies in early to mid-April, and maincrops from mid-April into early May.

They are worth chitting, especially the earlies, so they are already sprouting when they go into the ground. A colder garden should plant later than a mild one. Gardeners' World suggests delaying planting by a couple of weeks in northerly areas.

calendar.label: Chit
calendar.detail: Start in late January in milder areas, and up to early March in colder spots. The RHS says the process takes four to six weeks.

calendar.label: Plant
calendar.detail: First earlies around late March, second earlies in early to mid-April, maincrops from mid-April to early May.

calendar.label: Harvest
calendar.detail: First earlies in June and July, second earlies in July and August, maincrops from August to October.

sowOutdoors: Stand seed potatoes in a tray or egg box with the eyes upwards, in a bright, frost-free place. The RHS says chitting is not essential, but it is worthwhile for first and second earlies if you want an earlier crop.

Plant into a trench about 15cm deep, or into individual holes, with the sprouts facing up. Cover them carefully so you do not knock the sprouts off. First earlies go in around late March, second earlies in early to mid-April, and maincrops from mid-April to early May. If the soil is wet, the RHS notes you can wait. A mid-April planting still crops, just a little later.
plantOut: Potatoes are planted as tubers rather than transplanted as seedlings. If a late frost is forecast after the shoots appear, draw soil over the leaves or cover the row. Frosted foliage often grows back.

Earth up once the shoots are about 23cm tall. Draw soil up around the stems to form a ridge, leaving the top 10cm of the plants in the light, and repeat a few weeks apart until the ridge is 20 to 30cm high. It stops tubers pushing into the light and turning green, and it protects new shoots from a cold night.

If you are short of space, early varieties are the ones for containers. The RHS suggests a pot at least 30cm wide and deep. Half-fill it with about 15cm of peat-free compost, plant one seed potato per 30cm of pot diameter, and add more compost as the shoots grow.
harvest: First earlies are ready in June and July. Feel for tubers about the size of a hen's egg and lift a plant at a time. They do not store well, so dig what you will eat.

Second earlies follow in July and August. Maincrops are lifted from August to October, once the leaves have yellowed. Choose a dry day, leave the tubers on the surface for a few hours to dry, and store sound ones in paper or hessian somewhere cool, dark and frost-free. Cut diseased tops off and do not store damaged tubers.

problems.title: Green tubers
text: Light turns tubers green, and green potatoes are poisonous. Earth up so the tubers stay covered, and do not eat green ones. This is the same reason containers need topping up as the plants grow.

problems.title: Blight
text: Potatoes are closely related to tomatoes and, outdoors, they are similarly susceptible to blight. Warm, wet spells are when it spreads. If the foliage collapses with blight, cut it off and lift the crop rather than leaving infected tops over the tubers.

problems.title: Frosted shoots
text: A May frost can blacken young leaves. Cover the row when a cold night is forecast. Plants usually grow back from lower buds, though it sets the crop back.

steps.name: Chit the tubers
steps.text: From late January in mild areas, up to early March in colder ones, sprout seed potatoes in a bright frost-free place for four to six weeks.

steps.name: Plant in spring
steps.text: Plant first earlies around late March, second earlies in early to mid-April and maincrops from mid-April to early May, about 15cm deep.

steps.name: Earth up
steps.text: When shoots are about 23cm tall, draw soil up around the stems, leaving about 10cm of leaf showing. Repeat a few weeks apart.

steps.name: Harvest by type
steps.text: Lift first earlies in June and July, second earlies in July and August, and maincrops from August to October.

faqs.question: When should I plant seed potatoes in the UK?
answer: First earlies around late March, second earlies in early to mid-April and maincrops from mid-April to early May. Go a little later in cold or northern gardens and a little earlier in mild ones, and cover the shoots if a frost is forecast after they come up.

faqs.question: Can I plant a potato from the supermarket?
answer: Use certified seed potatoes. Supermarket tubers are not sold for planting, and they may not suit UK conditions or be free of disease. The same warning is made for supermarket garlic.

faqs.question: Do I have to chit potatoes?
answer: No. The RHS says chitting is optional. It is most useful for early varieties, because those sprouted tubers crop sooner. Maincrops will still grow if you plant them unsprouted.

guide.title: When to plant seed potatoes
intro: Seed potatoes go in from late March to early May, in order of type. The RHS dates below suit a typical UK season. Plant slightly later in colder regions and earlier in milder ones. Gardeners' World suggests a delay of a couple of weeks in northerly areas. Young shoots are easily damaged by frost in April and May, so choose an open plot that is not a frost pocket and check the last frost window for your area.

Not needed. The RHS sees no real advantage

paragraphs: Earlies that you did not chit still grow perfectly well. The RHS says they just take a few weeks longer to crop. If the soil is wet at planting time, waiting is better than forcing tubers into cold mud.

Two RHS options fall outside the main season. For an extra-early crop, plant chitted earlies at the beginning of March in large containers in a frost-free greenhouse, for new potatoes by about mid-May. For a Christmas crop, plant prepared cold-stored seed potatoes in July or early August in a large container in a greenhouse or another bright, frost-free place.
Seed potatoes are on sale in late winter and spring. Mail-order suppliers let you order in advance, which helps because popular varieties can sell out.
